transcript: If you haven't seen Little Shop of horrors or just haven't been in a while, now is a really good time to visit. Ever since this show opened, my top dream cast has been Betsy Wolfe as Audrey. So when they announced that she was finally going to be doing the show and with Ethan Slater as Seymour, I was like, I have to be there. And I am happy to report that they did not disappoint. Ethan brings this perfect, nerdy, awkward energy to Seymour, and Betsy manages to create an Audrey that is quirky and funny, but doesn't feel like a caricature. It is a really tough needle to thread with that character, and I think she threads it beautifully. In fact, the entire cast, which includes Claybourne Elder, who you may know from the recent company revival, and Reg Rogers, who you may know from the recent merrily revival, is firing on all cylinders. I think this might just be the funniest the show has ever been. They're finding so many new moments of comedy in lines that have never been jokes before. The camp is just dialed up to 11, but they never lose the heart or the humanity underneath it. And what I love about Little Shop in general is that they really give the actors space to just make the roles their own. None of them feel like they are copying what came before. Particularly Reg Rogers as Mushnik, who is giving like One of the most unhinged performances in that role that I have ever seen. And yet it, like, somehow works. There is a reason why this production has run for as long as it has, and that is because it is a perfect production of a perfect musical. There is just something so special about seeing top tier Broadway talent in a super intimate, tiny 200 seat theatre performing some of the greatest show tunes ever written.
